title_en: Tang Jin v. Dangtu County Labor Bureau — dispute over failure to perform statutory duty to protect personal and property rights
keywords_en: administrative; failure to perform statutory duties; first instance; basic people's court; Anhui Province; natural person; state organ; labor law; administrative procedure law; whether statutory duties have been performed; whether the act of forwarding and approving constitutes performance of duties; support for plaintiff; labor inspection; written application; failure to respond; administrative litigation
full_text_en:
Tang Jin v. Dangtu County Labor Bureau — dispute over failure to perform statutory duty to protect personal and property rights

Plaintiff: Tang Jin, male, 36 years old, an employee of Dangtu County Building Materials Company, Anhui Province.

Defendant: Dangtu County Labor Bureau, Anhui Province.

Legal Representative: Guan Qicai, Director.

The plaintiff, Tang Jin, initiated an administrative lawsuit with the Dangtu County People's Court on the ground that the defendant, Dangtu County Labor Bureau, had failed to perform its statutory duty to protect personal and property rights.

Plaintiff's Allegations: The plaintiff submitted a written application to Dangtu County Labor Bureau, requesting the Bureau to perform its statutory duty to protect the lawful rights and interests of laborers and to provide a reply. However, more than two months passed without the Bureau responding to the plaintiff's application. The plaintiff requests that the Bureau be ordered to perform its statutory duty.

Defendant's Defense: The defendant had forwarded the plaintiff's application as a letter from the public to Dangtu County Materials Bureau for handling, thereby lawfully performing its statutory duty. The plaintiff's lawsuit is unfounded.

Facts Found by the Court: The plaintiff, Tang Jin, wrote an application reflecting that his employer, Dangtu County Building Materials Company, had violated labor laws and regulations, abused its authority, suspended and wrongfully deducted his income, and requested that Dangtu County Labor Bureau investigate and handle the matter according to law. The application was mailed to Dangtu County Labor Bureau on January 1, 1996. On January 4, 1996, Guan Qicai, Director of Dangtu County Labor Bureau, endorsed the letter: "Forward this document to the Materials Bureau for handling." Thereafter, the Bureau neither conducted supervision or inspection of the issues raised in the application nor gave any reply to Tang Jin himself.

The above facts are confirmed by the statements of both parties and documentary evidence. The facts are clear, the evidence is true and sufficient, and the findings are well-established.

Opinion of the Court: Article 88, paragraph 2 of the Labor Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "Any organization or individual has the right to report and accuse acts violating labor laws and regulations." The plaintiff, Tang Jin, believing that the Building Materials Company had violated labor laws and regulations and infringed upon his lawful rights and interests, wrote a letter requesting investigation and handling, which is an exercise of a citizen's legitimate right. Article 9, paragraph 2 of the Labor Law provides: "The labor administrative departments of the local people's governments at or above the county level shall be in charge of labor work within their respective administrative areas." The defendant, Dangtu County Labor Bureau, is the department in charge of labor work within the administrative area of Dangtu County. It was appropriate for Tang Jin to lodge his complaint with it regarding labor work issues. Article 85 of the Labor Law provides: "The labor administrative departments of the people's governments at or above the county level shall, according to law, supervise and inspect the compliance of employers with labor laws and regulations, have the power to stop acts violating labor laws and regulations, and order corrections." Article 86 provides for the power of labor administrative departments to carry out supervision and inspection duties, and Chapter XII provides various powers for labor administrative departments to handle violations of labor laws and regulations by employers. These provisions indicate that Dangtu County Labor Bureau has both the duty and the power to supervise, inspect, and handle the compliance of employers with labor laws and regulations. Article 87 of the Labor Law provides: "The relevant departments of the people's governments at or above the county level shall, within their respective functions and duties, supervise the compliance of employers with labor laws and regulations." The Materials Bureau is a department of the people's government. It has the power to supervise the compliance of the Building Materials Company, which is under its purview, with labor laws and regulations, but it does not have the power to handle violations. When Dangtu County Labor Bureau forwarded the letter requesting investigation and handling of violations to the Materials Bureau, which had no authority to handle such matters, while itself neither performing the duty of supervision and inspection nor inquiring about the outcome of the Materials Bureau's supervision, and without replying to the letter writer, it cannot be deemed to have performed its statutory duty. If an administrative organ were allowed to simply forward a citizen's letter within its area of responsibility and consider its duty fulfilled, without the need to check, follow up, or reply to the letter writer, then the rights of citizens to report and accuse granted by law would become illusory. The Dangtu County Labor Bureau's defense that it had performed its statutory duty cannot be sustained. Accordingly, in accordance with Article 54, item (3) of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Dangtu County People's Court rendered the following judgment on April 23, 1996:

The defendant, Dangtu County Labor Bureau, is ordered to conduct supervision and inspection of the compliance of Dangtu County Building Materials Company with labor laws and regulations according to law, and to provide a written reply to the plaintiff, Tang Jin, within two months.

Court acceptance fee of RMB 100 and other litigation costs of RMB 200 shall be borne by the defendant, Dangtu County Labor Bureau.

After the judgment was pronounced, neither the plaintiff nor the defendant appealed. The judgment has become legally effective.
